chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'I would love it for the understanding man, when he intends to divorce his wife, that he should divorce her with the divorce of the Sunnah.'

He (Zurara) said: 'Then he (the Imam) said: And it is that which God — Mighty and Majestic — said: «Perhaps God will bring about a matter after that» — meaning after the divorce and the completion of the waiting period ('idda), the remarriage of both of them, before she marries another husband.'

He said: 'How just and how accommodating it is for them both together: that he divorce her in a state of ritual purity without intercourse, with a single pronouncement of divorce before witnesses, then leave her until her term expires — three months or three menstrual cycles — and then he may become one suitor among the suitors.'

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period ('idda) — the mandatory interval a divorced woman must observe before remarriage
key_terms.تَطْلِيقَةٌ: A single pronouncement of divorce — emphasizing revocability
key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Divorce of the Sunnah — the prescribed method of revocable repudiation following prophetic practice
key_terms.طُهْرٌ: State of ritual purity — free from menstruation; required for valid sunnaic divorce
key_terms.قُرُوءٌ: Quru' — ambiguous term meaning either menstrual cycles or periods of purity; used for measuring 'idda

ai.seo_question: What is the proper method of divorce according to the Sunnah in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Baqir (AS) explains the proper Sunnaic method of divorce (talaq al-sunnah) to Zurara, one of his most trusted companions and legal experts. The Imam cites Quran 65:1 to show that the prescribed divorce procedure — pronouncing a single revocable repudiation during the wife's period of ritual purity, without prior intercourse, in front of witnesses — keeps open the possibility of remarriage. This was addressed to scholars well-versed in jurisprudence, who would recognize the Imam's guidance as a practical elaboration of the divine wisdom behind the Quranic regulation.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would love it for the understanding man when he intends to divorce his wife that he should divorce her with a divorce of the Sunnah’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then heasws said: ‘And it is that which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says [65:1] Perhaps Allah may, after that, bring about a matter – Meaning, after the divorce and the fulfilling of the waiting period, the marriage of them both from before she marries another husband’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How much justice there is, and leeway for both of them together, that he divorces her upon purity from without copulation with a divorce by witnesses, then leaves her until her term is free with three months, or three menstruations, then he happens to be a proposer from the proposers’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’If a man wants to divorce his wife I like if he does so in the form of divorce according to Surinah.’

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) then said, ’This is that about which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, ’. . . perhaps Allah thereafter will cause something to happen.’ [65:2] It means after divorce and waiting period a marriage with him, before the advance of the case to a marriage with another man.

He (the Imam) said, ’How vast is the justice and time for them! He must divorce her in a Hayd (menses)-free period without sexual intercourse one divorce in the presence of witnesses then leave her until three months or three Hayd (menses) then he becomes one of those who may propose marriage.’”
